~~~{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
result_dir <- '../output/sst_chla_screen'
features <- read_csv('../data/processed/sst_chla_features_validation.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)
metrics <- read_csv(file.path(result_dir, 'metrics.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
metrics_2024 <- read_csv(file.path(result_dir, 'metrics_2024.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
predictions <- read_csv(file.path(result_dir, 'predictions.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
correlations <- read_csv(file.path(result_dir, 'correlations.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)
pca_variance <- read_csv(file.path(result_dir, 'pca_variance.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE)

programme_labels <- c(manta = 'Manta tow', ltmp = 'LTMP', mmp = 'MMP')
candidate_labels <- c(
  core = 'Core',
  sst_chla_raw = 'Core + SST shape + chlorophyll',
  modifier_pca = 'Modifier PCA'
)
learner_labels <- c(brt = 'BRT', inla = 'INLA')

metrics <- metrics |>
  mutate(
    Programme = recode(programme_key, !!!programme_labels),
    Candidate = recode(candidate, !!!candidate_labels),
    Learner = recode(learner, !!!learner_labels),
    Validation = recode(
      scheme,
      reef_blocked_5fold = 'Reef-blocked',
      leave_one_event_out = 'Event-held-out'
    )
  )
metrics_2024 <- metrics_2024 |>
  mutate(
    Programme = recode(programme_key, !!!programme_labels),
    Candidate = recode(candidate, !!!candidate_labels),
    Learner = recode(learner, !!!learner_labels)
  )
~~~

## Decision summary

The requested features are now reproducibly extracted and screened. They are
ecologically plausible and add information not identical to DHW, but they do
not yet produce a stable improvement across programmes, learners, and both
blocked validation schemes. They should remain in the candidate pool, not enter
the operational BRMS–BRT model as a universal addition.

The clearest positive results are spatially blocked rather than event-held-out.
For LTMP, raw SST shape plus wet-season chlorophyll improves BRT reef-blocked
RMSE from 0.133 to 0.127, and 2024 RMSE from 0.121 to 0.107. For MMP,
modifier PCA improves BRT reef-blocked RMSE from 0.266 to 0.250. Neither
signal generalises cleanly when a whole event is held out; manta tow retains
the core INLA model as the best reef-blocked result.

This split is a useful warning: the new metrics may distinguish reefs within
observed events, but their apparent benefit may partly encode event-specific
conditions. They need testing together with rainfall, coloured water, cyclone
exposure, wind, COTS and cooling relief before we decide whether they describe
an independent ecological process or proxy one.

## Data and feature definitions

NOAA Coral Reef Watch CoralTemp v3.1 supplies daily, gap-free, 5-km nighttime
SST. IMOS MODIS-Aqua OC3 supplies daily chlorophyll-a (mg m^-3^) through 25
December 2024. OC3 is primary because it is the standard NASA ocean-colour
algorithm. The extractor retains enough provenance to repeat this using OCI as
a coastal-water sensitivity.

| Feature | Window | Role |
|---|---|---|
| SST summer skewness | 1 Nov previous year–30 Apr event year | Acute summer SST trajectory asymmetry |
| SST summer excess kurtosis | Same | Distributional concentration/tails |
| Prior-year SST moments | Complete previous year | PCA sensitivity only |
| Wet-season Chl-a median | 1 Dec previous year–30 Apr event year | Primary Chl-a exposure |
| Q1 Chl-a median | 1 Jan–31 Mar | Sensitivity aligned with cloud/Secchi |

SST uses the nearest CRW cell. Chlorophyll uses the nearest valid water pixel
within 5 km when a reef centroid is masked. Wet-season Chl-a is primary because
it has complete coverage in every validation reef-year; Q1 alone is missing for
a small number.

~~~{r}
features |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    reef_years = n(),
    complete_summer_sst = percent(mean(sst_summer_n >= 181), accuracy = 0.1),
    wet_chl_coverage = percent(mean(is.finite(chla_wetseason_median)), accuracy = 0.1),
    wet_chl_observations = median(chla_wetseason_n),
    q1_chl_coverage = percent(mean(is.finite(chla_q1_median)), accuracy = 0.1),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |>
  kable(caption = 'Extraction coverage for validation reef-years.')
~~~

## Complementarity and PCA

PCA is a diagnostic for correlated information, not a selection rule by itself.
Current DHW, coral cover/composition and exposure history remain direct,
interpretable effects. PCA is restricted to environmental modifiers and is
learnt within each analysis fold.

~~~{r}
feature_order <- c(
  'ann_maxdhw', 'dhw10_load4', 'dhw_novelty10', 'secc3m_p10', 'cloudp_90',
  'sst_summer_skewness', 'sst_summer_excess_kurtosis',
  'sst_prevyear_skewness', 'sst_prevyear_excess_kurtosis',
  'chla_wetseason_median'
)

correlations |>
  filter(feature_1 %in% feature_order, feature_2 %in% feature_order) |>
  mutate(
    feature_1 = factor(feature_1, levels = feature_order),
    feature_2 = factor(feature_2, levels = rev(feature_order))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(feature_1, feature_2, fill = spearman_rho)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf('%.2f', spearman_rho)), size = 2.7) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = '#2166ac', mid = 'white', high = '#b2182b',
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = 'Modifier correlations show redundancy and independent axes',
    subtitle = 'Spearman correlation across validation reef-years',
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = 'rho'
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
~~~

Wet-season and Q1 Chl-a are almost duplicates (rho = 0.97); only wet-season
median is direct. Summer skewness and kurtosis are related (rho = -0.78) but
not duplicates, so both remain in the raw ecological candidate.

~~~{r}
pca_variance |>
  mutate(
    Programme = recode(programme_key, !!!programme_labels),
    Component = factor(component, levels = paste0('PC', 1:8))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(Component, cumulative_variance, group = Programme, colour = Programme)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.85, linetype = 2, colour = 'grey40') +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(shape = retained), size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = 'Four modifier PCs pass the 85% variance rule',
    subtitle = 'Full-data audit; every prediction fold learns its own PCA',
    x = NULL, y = 'Cumulative variance explained', colour = NULL, shape = 'Retained'
  )
~~~

The leading PC combines summer SST shape with chronic heat load. A separate PC
is dominated by Secchi and wet-season chlorophyll. This is useful as a
sensitivity because it represents shared axes without claiming that every
correlated variable has a separately identifiable effect.

## Blocked predictive screen

The same outer folds as the formal models were used. BRT complexity and INLA
priors are fixed across candidate sets for a fair feature screen. A promoted
candidate would still need nested tuning and formal BRMS refitting.

~~~{r}
metrics |>
  select(Programme, Learner, Validation, Candidate, rows, rmse, mae,
         predictive_r2, bias, occurrence_brier, severe_bias) |>
  arrange(Learner, Validation, Programme, rmse) |>
  mutate(across(c(rmse, mae, predictive_r2, bias, occurrence_brier, severe_bias), round, 3)) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c('Programme', 'Learner', 'Validation', 'Candidate', 'n',
                  'RMSE', 'MAE', 'Predictive R2', 'Bias', 'Brier', 'Severe bias'),
    caption = 'Blocked performance; severe bias is prediction minus observation at mortality >=50%.'
  )
~~~

~~~{r}
deltas <- metrics |>
  group_by(programme_key, Learner, Validation) |>
  mutate(delta_rmse = rmse - rmse[Candidate == 'Core']) |>
  filter(Candidate != 'Core') |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(deltas, aes(Programme, delta_rmse, fill = Candidate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = 'grey40') +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  facet_grid(Learner ~ Validation) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    'Core + SST shape + chlorophyll' = '#1b9e77',
    'Modifier PCA' = '#7570b3'
  )) +
  labs(
    title = 'No candidate improves consistently under spatial and temporal blocking',
    subtitle = 'Negative values improve RMSE relative to core',
    x = NULL, y = 'Change in RMSE', fill = NULL
  )
~~~

## 2024 behaviour

~~~{r}
metrics_2024 |>
  select(Programme, Learner, Candidate, rows, rmse, mae, predictive_r2,
         bias, severe_rows, severe_bias) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3)) |>
  arrange(Learner, Programme, rmse) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c('Programme', 'Learner', 'Candidate', 'n', 'RMSE', 'MAE',
                  'Predictive R2', 'Bias', 'Severe n', 'Severe bias'),
    caption = 'Reef-blocked performance within the 2024 event.'
  )
~~~

~~~{r}
predictions |>
  filter(scheme == 'reef_blocked_5fold', event_year == 2024) |>
  mutate(
    Programme = recode(programme_key, !!!programme_labels),
    Candidate = recode(candidate, !!!candidate_labels),
    Learner = recode(learner, !!!learner_labels)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(observed_mortality, predicted_mortality, colour = Candidate)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = 'grey45', linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.6) +
  facet_grid(Learner ~ Programme) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    'Core' = '#666666',
    'Core + SST shape + chlorophyll' = '#1b9e77',
    'Modifier PCA' = '#7570b3'
  )) +
  labs(
    title = 'New features do not yet resolve severe-loss shrinkage',
    subtitle = '2024 out-of-sample reef predictions',
    x = 'Observed mortality', y = 'Predicted mortality', colour = NULL
  )
~~~

The additions reduce some 2024 error, especially in LTMP and MMP, but severe
mortality remains strongly underpredicted. They are not substitutes for compound
stressors or better community-composition resolution.

## Recommended next stage

1. Retain wet-season median OC3 Chl-a as the one direct chlorophyll candidate;
   do not also add Q1 Chl-a.
2. Retain summer SST skewness and excess kurtosis as a grouped candidate.
3. Keep modifier PCA as a sensitivity rather than the primary ecological model.
4. Join compound stressors, then repeat this screen with nested tuning for the
   few candidates that improve both spatial and temporal blocking.
5. Promote only stable candidates to exact BRMS and production BRT refits.

The extractor can now point at the all-GBR feature grid when a candidate earns
promotion; its per-year caches make that operational run restartable.
